The men's senior selection committee, chaired by Ajit Agarkar, announced the 15-member squad for the two-Test series against Sri Lanka, starting August 15 in Galle. Ravindra Jadeja, who was rested for the Afghanistan Test, returns to the squad, while off-spinner Saransh Jain has earned his maiden call-up as Washington Sundar remains unavailable for the first Test.Injury concerns persist, with both Sai Sudharsan and Jasprit Bumrah selected pending fitness clearance from the BCCI CoE. Otherwise, the squad is largely on expected lines, with the core batting group retained. The seam attack features the usual names: Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Bumrah and Gurnoor Brar, who retained his spot after a strong performance against Sri Lanka A.For the spin department, Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav are expected to shoulder the responsibility alongside Manav Suthar and Saransh Jain. Suthar impressed against Afghanistan, while Jain was preferred as the specialist off-spinner in Sundar's absence.The 33-year-old has played 54 First-Class matches and was on the selectors' radar. They handed him an India A opportunity during the recent tour of Sri Lanka. He chipped in with six wickets and an unbeaten 70 in the final game.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that the selectors are unwilling to take any fitness-related risks for the series, and both Sudharsan and Bumrah will feature only if they clear all fitness benchmarks at the CoE.It is understood that Bumrah should be fit for the opening Test in Galle, but even with a one percent doubt, the think tank will not rush a half-fit player back into the playing XI.India are expected to reach Sri Lanka early in the first week of August before preparing for a four-day warm-up fixture in Colombo, starting August 7.Shubman Gill (C), KL Rahul (VC), Yashasvi Jaiswal Rishabh Pant (WK), Sai Sudharsan*, Dhruv Jurel (WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav, Manav Suthar, Jasprit Bumrah*, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Devdutt Padikkal, Saransh Jain.Note:

Article Title: 'I was beaten from 11 pm to 3 am': How Sharmila Dhankar overcame marriage abuse to script CWG history
Article Text:
Sharmila Dhankar (ANI Photo)

New Delhi:

For Sharmila Dhankar, every throw carries the weight of a life rebuilt. From growing up in poverty in Haryana’s Mahendragarh district and surviving domestic abuse in her first marriage to selling the family home to sustain her sporting dream, the 40-year-old para shot putter has turned adversity into ambition as she prepares for her second Commonwealth Games (CWG).On Monday night, Sharmila scripted history by becoming India's first-ever COmmonwealth Games para-athletics gold medallist. She delivered a landmark performance by winning the women's shot put F57 title with a season-best effort of 9.81m, ending the nation's 20-year wait for a para-athletics medal at the Games. The last para-athletics medal in CWG was won by Ranjith Kumar Jayaseelan in the men's seated discus throw event in the 2006 edition.The F57 classification is for athletes with lower limb impairments, limb deficiencies or reduced muscle power.The seated thrower, who also competes in discus, headed into the Games on the back of an impressive showing at the Fazza International Para Athletics Championship in Dubai, where she won gold in shot put and bronze in discus.Her sporting journey began only at the age of 34. Sharmila contracted polio at the age of two, affecting her right leg and grew up in a family struggling to make ends meet.“My mother was blind, my father was a farmer and we had very little to survive. Life was never easy,” she told TOI.Married at 19, she endured years of domestic violence before returning to her parents’ home with her two daughters — Anju, now 15, and Lakshmi, 13. “One night, I was beaten from 11 pm to 3 am by my first husband and thrown out of the house. I never went back,” she recalled.Her life changed after her second marriage. Husband Ajit Singh introduced her to para sports and encouraged her to train under coaches Tek Chand and Devendra. In 2021, she made her debut at the Para National Championships and won gold with a national record.The following year, she finished fourth at the Birmingham CWG, narrowly missing a medal. She placed fourth again at the Asian Para Games in Hangzhou in 2023. Despite those strong performances, financial hardship persisted. To fund her career, the family sold their house in Rewari in 2023 and moved into rented accommodation. “Sport has given me a second birth. After winning medals in para CWG and Asian Games this year, I want to buy a house again,” she said.Sharmila had finished fifth at the World Para Athletics Championships in New Delhi last year. Beyond medals, her biggest dream is to ensure that her daughters have the opportunities she never did. Both are budding athletes — Anju competes in the under-16 javelin throw, while Lakshmi is an under-14 long jumper. Sharmila hopes sport will help them build a future free from the hardships she had to overcome.
Article Summary: Sharmila Dhankar became India's first-ever COmmonwealth Games para-athletics gold medallist. She delivered a landmark performance by winning the women's shot put F57 title with a season-best effort of 9.81m. The 40-year-old para shot putter has turned adversity into ambition.

Article Title: 'If he gets his length right': Glenn McGrath backs one India pacer as Jasprit Bumrah's long-term partner
Article Text:
India's Prasidh Krishna with his teammates celebrates (ANI Photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view Should selectors consider veteran bowlers like Shami for future games? Yes, experience can be valuable No, focus on younger talent 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Chennai: As India look to usher in a new generation of fast bowlers, Australian great Glenn McGrath believes Prasidh Krishna has all the ingredients to become Jasprit Bumrah 's long-term pace partner.The legendary fast bowler, who is the director of coaching at the MRF Pace Foundation, has closely followed Prasidh's rise and feels the tall Karnataka seamer has transformed his potential into performances."I'm a big fan of Prasidh," McGrath said. "If he gets his length right, he's got everything going for him.""He has really matured. He's tall, bowls in good areas, generates bounce and has genuine pace. Occasionally he's a little short, but apart from that, I think he's the whole package. He's really developed and put his potential into performance," he said.India have handed opportunities to several young quicks during the recent tours of the UK and Zimbabwe as they prepare for a demanding cycle of white-ball cricket, with the ODI and T20 World Cups to be played in South Africa and Australia-New Zealand respectively. It means India will need a strong pace attack firing on all cylinders, and McGrath believes the transition phase they are going through will not be easy."You've got Bumrah , who's a class bowler, and Mohammed Shami , who's world-class as well. Mohammed Siraj has been around for a long time too. You can't just expect to pick up straight where you left off. It's always going to be a transitional period," he said, referring to the Australian team, which will also go through a similar phase."Other than Pat Cummins , Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc , hardly anybody gets a chance... So it's not going to be easy for Australia either."McGrath also pointed out that Bumrah's unconventional action demands careful workload management."The way he powers through those last few steps probably puts more stress on his body than most bowlers. It'll be interesting to see how he manages himself," McGrath said.While India appear keen to fast-track younger bowlers, McGrath insisted experienced pacers still have an important role to play."It's always good to have experience there. Young bowlers learn by playing alongside senior guys. I was fortunate to watch Craig McDermott and Merv Hughes. That's where you really learn. I'd always pick an experienced team over a potential team," he said.On whether veterans such as Shami or Bhuvneshwar Kumar could still mount a comeback, McGrath said the decision rested on their bodies, motivation and the selectors."If they're prepared to put the work in and their body allows it, then why not? As fast bowlers get older, the work only gets tougher. Ultimately, it's up to them and the selectors."McGrath also called for a rethink in the way fast bowlers are rehabilitated after injuries, arguing that modern systems often "wrap bowlers in cotton wool" instead of making them physically stronger."The best way is to get stronger. Even when you're injured, you should keep working on the parts of the body that you can train. Instead of protecting bowlers, we should be making them unbreakable," he said.
Article Summary: Glenn McGrath believes Prasidh Krishna has all the ingredients to become Jasprit Bumrah's long-term pace partner. India have handed opportunities to several young quicks during the recent tours of the UK and Zimbabwe. McGrath insisted experienced pacers still have an important role to play.

Article Title: Tennis legend Novak Djokovic teams up with Aryna Sabalenka for revamped US Open mixed doubles
Article Text:
Novak Djokovic teams up with Aryna Sabalenka (Photo by Getty Images)

How the tournament will work

USTA backs revamped format



NEW DELHI: Novak Djokovic will partner with Aryna Sabalenka as top tennis stars headline the initial list of 16 teams which have entered this year's revamped US Open mixed doubles championship.The event, which offers a $1 million prize to the winning pair, has once again attracted many of the biggest names in singles tennis after its successful relaunch last year.Among the notable entries are Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud, last year's runners-up, Elena Rybakina and Taylor Fritz, Naomi Osaka and Kei Nishikori, and Jessica Pegula and Jack Draper.Defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori have also entered, although they are likely to require a wild card again because of their lower singles rankings.The main draw will take place over two days, August 25-26, with all matches scheduled at Arthur Ashe Stadium and Louis Armstrong Stadium.Six teams with the best combined singles rankings after entries close on August 17 will qualify automatically, while eight teams will receive wild cards and two more will earn their places through a qualifying event on August 24.The revamped format, introduced last year, drew criticism for favouring singles players over doubles specialists.However, it proved popular with fans, attracting around 78,000 spectators and sell-out crowds on both days.USTA CEO Craig Tiley believes the event has added a fresh dimension to the Grand Slam."Any time you can bring women and men together on the same team, you showcase tennis at its best. This is exactly what the mixed doubles championship does," he said."The mixed doubles championship is an innovation that will engage new audiences and give our fans another opportunity to see the biggest stars compete together."The qualifying tournament has also created more opportunities for doubles specialists this year. Matches up to the semifinals will be played in a shortened best-of-three format, while the final will follow traditional scoring with full six-game sets.
Article Summary: Novak Djokovic teams up with Aryna Sabalenka for US Open mixed doubles. 16 teams have entered this year's event, which offers a $1 million prize. Last year's runners-up Elena Rybakina and Taylor Fritz are among the other entries.

Article Title: Commonwealth Games: Bindyarani Devi wins bronze; India claims fifth weightlifting medal in Glasgow
Article Text:
India's Devi Bindyarani Sorokhibam competes in the 58 kilogram category of women weightlifting during the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, Monday, July 27, 2026. (AP Photo)

India's weightlifting contingent added another Commonwealth Games medal on Sunday as Bindyarani Devi clinched Bronze in the women's 58kg final.It was India's fifth weightlifting medal at the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Earlier, Mirabai Chanu (women's 48kg - gold), Rishikanta Singh (men's 60kg - silver), Muthupandi Raja (men's 65kg - silver), and Gyaneshwari Yadav (women's 53kg - silver) had also finished on the podium in their respective categories.Weightlifting comprises two disciplines — the snatch and the clean and jerk — with each lifter getting three attempts in both.In the snatch, athletes lift the barbell from the ground to overhead in one continuous movement with a wide grip. In the clean and jerk, they first lift the bar to their shoulders (clean), pause, and then drive it overhead (jerk), holding it steady until the buzzer.Bindyarani lifted 87kg in the snatch to finish third. Nigeria's Rafiatu Folashade led the field with 103kg, while Canada's Ann Sophie was second with 83kg.In the clean and jerk, Bindyarani successfully lifted 112kg. However, Rafiatu managed 122kg to retain her lead and secure the gold medal, leaving the Indian lifter with bronze.Bindyarani totalled 199kg (87kg snatch + 112g clean and jerk) but Nigeria's Rafiatu Folashade stole the show with a stunning 225kg (103kg + 122kg), rewriting both the Commonwealth and Commonwealth Games records to take the gold.Canada's Ann Sophie won the silver medal with 215 kg (94+121)It is the fifth weightlifting medal for India at the CWG and sixth medal overall.
Article Summary: Bindyarani Devi clinched Bronze in the women's 58kg final. It is India's fifth weightlifting medal at the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Nigeria's Rafiatu Folashade stole the show with a stunning 225kg (103kg + 122kg)

Article Title: Rohit Sharma remains 'irreplaceable' for India's 2027 World Cup plans, says former cricketer
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be India's primary focus leading up to the 2027 World Cup? Building on the current squad Experimenting with new players 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Former India batter Aakash Chopra has said Rohit Sharma remains "irreplaceable" in India's ODI side as long as he is fit, available and continues to score runs in the build-up to the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.Questions over Rohit's future grew during India's tour of England. Ahead of the third ODI at Lord's, there was speculation that the series decider could be his last international appearance after he had already retired from T20Is and Tests. However, Rohit responded with a 138-run knock during India's chase of 388, ending doubts over his form.Speaking on The Great Indian Cricket Show on Doordarshan, Chopra said India's ODI plans should continue to revolve around the experienced opener."As long as Rohit Sharma is fit, available, and scoring runs, he remains irreplaceable. We are talking about sheer pedigree and legacy here. You do not need to look anywhere else in ODI cricket right now. We should not forget that the next World Cup is in South Africa, where conditions demand experienced heads who have been there, done that, and delivered under pressure," he said, as quoted by news agency ANI.Chopra also backed India's current opening combination of Rohit and ODI captain Shubman Gill, saying there is no reason to make changes."Right now, the opening pairing with Shubman Gill is working seamlessly, so why tinker with something that isn't broken? Often, when you have an abundance of options, there's a temptation to try something new just for the sake of it. But no matter how tempting those alternatives look, do not distract yourself. Keep the focus entirely on the World Cup, and as long as Rohit is here, Rohit stays," he said.Rohit finished the England ODI series with 175 runs in three matches at an average of 58.33 and a strike rate of 98.31. His highlight was a 138-run innings from 110 balls, including 17 fours and five sixes, during India's chase of 388 in the third ODI. India lost the match by 27 runs and the series 2-1, but Rohit's century stand with Virat Kohli , who scored 74 off 60 balls with four fours and three sixes, was one of the positives.Overall, Rohit has scored 11,895 runs in 288 ODIs and 280 innings at an average of 48.95 and a strike rate of 93.04. He has 34 centuries, 62 fifties and a highest score of 264. He is the seventh-highest run-scorer in ODI history and India's third-highest after Virat Kohli (14,941) and Sachin Tendulkar (18,426).In nine ODIs this year, Rohit has scored 379 runs at an average of 42.11, including one century and one fifty, with a highest score of 138.Rohit and Kohli are next expected to play in India's home ODI series against the West Indies, scheduled from September 27 to October 3.
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma remains "irreplaceable" in India's ODI side, says Aakash Chopra. Chopra says India's plans should continue to revolve around the experienced opener. Rohit finished the England ODI series with 175 runs in three matches at an average of 58.33.

Article Title: Ajaya Babu wins silver in 79kg weightlifting after record-breaking duel at Commonwealth Games
Article Text:
Erry Hidayat Muhammad of Malaysia with his gold medal alongside Valluri Ajaya Babu of India with his silver medal, left, and Chris Murray of England with his bronze medal, right. (AP)

Fast-rising Indian weightlifter Valluri Ajaya Babu won the silver medal in the men's 79kg category at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, adding another medal to India's tally in the sport.The 21-year-old from Vizianagaram district in Andhra Pradesh lifted a Commonwealth Games record 149kg in the snatch and 181kg in the clean and jerk for a total of 330kg. He finished just one kilogram behind Malaysia's Erry Hidayat Muhammad, who won the gold with a Games record total of 331kg (147kg snatch + 184kg clean and jerk).England's Chris Murray claimed the bronze medal with a total lift of 325kg.The battle for gold went down to the final lifts in the clean and jerk. Hidayat first lifted 181kg to set a new Commonwealth Games record. Ajaya Babu then matched and bettered that effort by lifting 181kg in his final attempt, taking his total to 330kg. Hidayat responded with a successful lift of 184kg in his last attempt to regain the record and secure the gold medal.Earlier in the snatch, Ajaya Babu recovered after failing his second attempt at 149kg. He lifted the same weight in his third and final attempt to set a new Commonwealth Games record and finish first in the snatch standings ahead of Chris Murray (148kg) and Erry Hidayat Muhammad (147kg).Ajaya Babu opened the competition with a successful lift of 145kg in the snatch before finishing the section with the record lift.The silver medal was India's sixth medal in weightlifting at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.Ajaya Babu has been among India's top weightlifters in recent years. At the 2025 Commonwealth Championships in Ahmedabad, he won gold in the men's 79kg category with a personal-best total of 335kg (152kg snatch + 183kg clean and jerk), setting new championship records. That performance earned him direct qualification for the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.At the 2024 Commonwealth Championships in Suva, Fiji, he won gold medals in both the junior and senior men's 81kg categories.He also competed at the 2025 World Championships in Forde, Norway, where he finished 16th overall in a field of 39 lifters.
Article Summary: Valluri Ajaya Babu won the silver medal in the men's 79kg category at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 21-year-old from Vizianagaram district in Andhra Pradesh lifted a Commonwealth Games record 149kg in the snatch. He finished just one kilogram behind Malaysia's Erry Hidayat Muhammad who won the gold with a Games record total of 331kg.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers unfazed by baggage snag on arrival
Article Text:
Santiago Nieva (Image credit: X)

India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two-week multinational training camp in Belfast, but its final preparations were briefly disrupted when some boxers’ luggage failed to arrive ahead of Thursday’s opening ceremony.The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp, during which the boxers benefitted from quality sparring and competition-specific training. However, several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.Sources said officials from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chef-de-mission’s office were at the airport on Wednesday, coordinating with the airline to ensure the baggage reached the contingent before the ceremony. The boxing competition begins on Friday and runs until Aug 1.The incident, however, has not gone down well with the Boxing Federation of India (BFI). Sources said that after the issue surfaced, the federation asked the boxers to submit declarations stating that they would not speak to the media about internal team matters and would instead remain focused on their performances.Despite the logistical hiccup, the mood in the camp remains upbeat. “We are settling in well in Glasgow. We had a good camp in Belfast where everybody got quality sparring and proper preparations. The boxers are managing their weights well. We will have the draws soon. We are coming with high expectations for this competition,” India women’s head coach Santiago Nieva told TOI .India’s 14-member squad features Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Jaismine Lamboria, the world No. 1 in the women’s 57kg category.
Article Summary: India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two- week multinational training camp in Belfast. The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp. Article Title: 'No one will tell me how to bat': Sanju Samson's vow to 'not be part of the rat race'
Article Text:
Sanju Samson

Senior India wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson has said he decided even before the 2026 T20 World Cup that he would stop worrying about outside opinions and play cricket on his own terms. He added that he no longer wants to be part of the "rat race" and will continue to trust his own instincts.Samson, who scored three consecutive fifties as India retained the Men's T20 World Cup title earlier this year, was later left out of the Zimbabwe tour after a dip in form during the Ireland and England series."I realised that there is a constant rat race in our country, and I decided before the 2026 T20 World Cup that I would not be part of it. I just want to enjoy the game. By God's grace, I have achieved a lot. I am 31 now, and I have a few years left. So, I have decided to play on my own terms. No one will tell me how to bat or what to do. Sanju will decide for Sanju."“With all due respect, I will play, enjoy the game, be a good teammate, and support the group, but I will do it my way. After the 2024 World Cup, I didn't even expect to play in the 2026 World Cup. I wasn't in the 14 or 15-man squad at one point. So how can I plan for 2028? If I'm there, if the team needs me, and if I'm playing well, things will fall into place.If not, I am deeply grateful. No one can take this achievement away from me," Samson said on JioStar, as quoted by news agency IANS.Samson also recalled a conversation with former India captain Virat Kohli during a national team camp, saying Kohli advised him to focus on discipline and lifestyle to build a long international career."We all know how Virat bhai is. He is very clear and very straightforward with everyone. If you need to do something, he will tell you exactly what is required. The way he carries himself in the gym, there is a different fire in that guy and I really love that about him.“We both were working out together in the gym during an Indian team camp and I asked him, 'Paaji, what should I do? Tell me something too!' and he told me that lifestyle plays a huge role. If you want to become an international cricketer, you must maintain a different kind of lifestyle.“He shared what works for him on his journey and told me, 'This food will help your body recover, this won't. If you maintain this discipline for the next 10 years, you will have a great career ahead.' I started following it for a year, a year, and a half, but after that, I couldn't stay on track with that anymore!" he explained.Speaking about India's T20 World Cup semi-final against England at the Wankhede Stadium, Samson said he ignored discussions about his previous record against England fast bowler Jofra Archer because he believed he had improved as a batter."When you score runs for the Indian team, you become more responsible, knowing you have to keep scoring. Ahead of the T20 World Cup semi-final against England, our top order wasn't firing much. A lot of people were coming and telling me, 'It's England, Archer is bowling, he got you out 3-4 times previously, this happened, that happened.'“But I was confident. I didn't say anything out loud. If you talk too much, you come across as arrogant, and that goes against my belief. So, I just gestured quietly, 'Yeah, we'll see.' But I had my plans ready. I knew that this Sanju Samson was not the Sanju Samson from a year ago. After that West Indies knock, I had a lot of self-validation, and I was very sure about myself. There was no room for doubt. I was going to do it for my country, and no one could stop it. ”Looking back at the World Cup final against New Zealand, Samson said he felt responsible for carrying India's batting after becoming the team's main run-scorer during the tournament."One thing I have learned is that you can't control form all the time. Form comes and goes. At that moment in our team setup, I was the one getting runs.“The others at the other end were contributing too, but much of the run-scoring burden was on me. I could feel the responsibility of being the main run-scorer in the World Cup final against New Zealand.“I kept reminding myself, 'Sanju, you are responsible. You need to keep going. You must stay there till the end and finish the job for your country.' That thought kept me focused throughout the innings," he elaborated.
Article Summary: Senior India wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson has said he would stop worrying about outside opinions and play cricket on his own terms. Samson said he no longer wants to be part of the "rat race" and will continue to trust his own instincts. Samson scored three consecutive fifties as India retained the Men's T20 World Cup title earlier this year.

Article Title: Lopes Cabral's curling goal against Argentina voted FIFA World Cup's best goal
Article Text:
Cape Verde's Sidny Lopes Cabral, celebrates scoring his side's second goal against Argentina during the World Cup round of 32 football match in Miami Gardens, Fla., Friday, July 3, 2026. (AP Photo)

Cape Verde added another chapter to its World Cup journey on Monday after Sidny Lopes Cabral won the public vote for the Goal of the Tournament.Lopes Cabral earned the honour for his curling strike into the top corner against Argentina during the 2026 FIFA World Cup . The goal came in extra time of Cape Verde's Round of 32 match in Miami Gardens, drawing his side level at 2-2 against the defending champions. Argentina, however, went on to win the match 3-2.The 2026 edition marked Cape Verde's first appearance at the FIFA World Cup. The African side progressed from the group stage before exiting in the Round of 32 against Argentina.Lopes Cabral's effort was voted the best among the 308 goals scored during the tournament. It finished ahead of Eldor Shomurodov's lob for Uzbekistan against Congo and Wilson Isidor's rising strike for Haiti against Morocco.FIFA shortlisted 12 goals for the public vote, which closed on Monday.Lopes Cabral's celebration also became one of the memorable moments of the tournament. After scoring, he broke away from teammates, climbed into the stands to hug his girlfriend and then searched for his mother.“Before the game, I’d told my mom and my girlfriend that if I scored, I’d run over to them,” he said. “When I got there, I saw my mom crying. She hadn’t even realized I was right there. Everyone was busy tending to her because she had fainted when I scored.”Their campaign began with a 0-0 draw against eventual champions Spain, with goalkeeper Vozinha playing a key role in the result.
Article Summary: Cape Verde's Sidny Lopes Cabral won the public vote for the Goal of the Tournament. His curling strike against Argentina during the 2026 FIFA World Cup was voted the best among the 308 goals scored during the tournament. The goal came in extra time, drawing his side level at 2-2 against the defending champions.

Article Title: Commonwealth Games: IOA issues health advisory amid Glasgow chill
Article Text:
Indian contingent pose as they arrive for the opening ceremony of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games (PTI Photo)

New Delhi :

With Glasgow hit by a sudden spell of cold, cloudy and rain-soaked weather, the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the country’s chef-de-mission office have advised athletes to take preventive measures to minimise the risk of upper respiratory and airborne infections during the Commonwealth Games.Sources told TOI that athletes have been verbally briefed at their respective hotels, with officials urging them to avoid unnecessary outdoor exposure, dress warmly and wear face masks while travelling or in crowded indoor spaces. Frequent hand washing has also been recommended as an added precaution.The advisory comes after temperatures dropped sharply over the past two days, making conditions considerably colder, especially during the evenings. A few Indian athletes have reported mild cold symptoms, including runny noses, but none has required hospitalisation.Officials stressed there is no cause for alarm, while underlining the importance of preventive care with several medal events still to come. “It is quite cold and cloudy here,” Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra said, reflecting the challenging weather conditions athletes have encountered in Glasgow.
Article Summary: Athletes advised to take preventive measures to minimise the risk of upper respiratory and airborne infections during the Commonwealth Games. A few Indian athletes have reported mild cold symptoms, including runny noses, but none has required hospitalisation. “It is quite cold and cloudy here,” Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra said.

The debate surrounding Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma 's ODI future refuses to die down despite both continuing to deliver for India. While neither head coach Gautam Gambhir nor chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar has publicly committed to their participation in the 2027 World Cup, keeping the speculation around their future alive.India's recent 1-2 ODI series defeat against England only added fuel to the conversation. Rohit silenced critics with a match-winning century in the series finale, registering his 34th ODI hundred amid speculation that the Lord's fixture could be his final international appearance. Kohli , meanwhile, chipped in with two half-centuries during the series after both senior batters struggled in the opening match.Former India wicketkeeper-batter Deep Dasgupta believes there is no need to question Rohit and Kohli's places in the side, but stressed that both must make an immediate impact whenever a series begins instead of taking time to settle.“That has to be a conversation with everyone, not just them (Kohli and Rohit), that they have to start the series well and hit the ground running. That is a challenge. You can’t take one or two games to get into the groove. But that’s where the support staff comes in and has conversations with the players by creating an environment to get the best out of everyone," Deep Dasgupta said on his YouTube channel.Dasgupta insisted that the standards applied to the two stalwarts should remain unchanged despite the increasing scrutiny around their careers.“There is no conversation needed with them about their places in the team. Four years back, it wasn’t like they had to be reminded before every series that they would be in the team. They knew they would be in the team based on their performances. So how does that change now? It does not and should not change,” he added.Questions over the future of Rohit and Kohli have surfaced repeatedly since both retired from Test cricket last year, leaving ODIs as their only international format. Before the Lord's ODI against England, reports suggested that the selection committee was considering moving on from Rohit ahead of the 2027 World Cup to create an opening for Yashasvi Jaiswal .However, the BCCI leadership dismissed reports that the Lord's encounter would be Rohit's final international appearance.Dasgupta believes the constant speculation is largely because the pair now feature in only one international format, making every ODI performance subject to greater scrutiny.“This discussion about their future is getting exaggerated because they play only one format. When you play multiple formats, if you fail in one but score in the other, the failure is forgotten. So that’s a challenge for these two that can’t be denied. People will remember what they last did in this format because they play only one format. But the conversation with them should be the same as it was three years ago,” he added.
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's ODI future remains under the spotlight. Both retired from Test cricket last year, leaving ODIs as their only international format. Former India wicketkeeper-batter Deep Dasgupta believes there is no need to question their places in the side. But he stressed that both must make an immediate impact whenever a series begins.

Article Title: 'Let Vaibhav Sooryavanshi open with Rohit Sharma': Ex-cricketer wants Shubman Gill to bat at No. 4
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma and Abhishek Sharma (Agency Image)

Former India wicketkeeper-batter Farokh Engineer believes teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already done enough to earn an ODI call-up and wants the 15-year-old to open alongside Rohit Sharma ahead of the 2027 World Cup.Engineer feels India should reshuffle their batting order by moving Shubman Gill to No. 4, allowing Sooryavanshi to partner Rohit at the top while Virat Kohli slots in at No. 3.“The ideal situation is Shubman Gill and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Gill is a class player. Gill, I think, is the best batsman in the team now. So, Gill should come at four,” Engineer told PTI.The former India star said the combination of a right-handed Rohit and left-handed Sooryavanshi would provide the ideal balance in ODI cricket.“Gill is not a guy who lifts the ball. So, a left-right combination would be ideal in ODIs. So, if Rohit is playing, and I think he should be playing, let him open with Sooryavanshi.“A batsman like him (Sooryavanshi) is much better at opening because he finds bigger gaps in the field. Virat Kohli can come third. Gill can come fourth and then we've got a solid batting line-up,” he said.Engineer's remarks come after Sooryavanshi enjoyed a breakthrough T20I series against Zimbabwe.The youngster finished as the leading run-scorer with 151 runs, including two half-centuries, and was named Player of the Series as India completed a 3-0 clean sweep.According to Engineer, those performances are enough to fast-track the teenager into India's 50-over plans.“This is probably the right time to draft Sooryavanshi into India's ODI side. I don't know why people distinguish so much between ODI and T20 because for me, a half-volley is a half-volley. He’s been getting runs and he's got the confidence to open the innings.“He'll win more matches for you than lose you. When he gives a start like that, the other players can have time to consolidate the innings and put on a big score,” Engineer noted.While Sooryavanshi struggled during India's T20I tour of England earlier this month, the Zimbabwe series showcased his ability to adapt. He produced a measured 81 off 49 balls in the final T20I on a slow Harare surface after blasting a rapid half-century in the series opener.The teenager has also shown areas that still require improvement, including handling short-pitched bowling, adapting quickly to overseas conditions and refining his shot selection. However, Engineer urged India not to overburden the youngster with technical changes, insisting his natural game is what makes him special.“Anything which is slightly short of length, in Sooryavanshi's curve, is going to go for a six. He learned from his mistakes, he has learned to curb himself. But don't try to over-coach him. He's not from the MCC book of manual, which is completely out of date.“He’s a genius. Nor was Viv Richards. Viv was the best batsman I've ever seen play. But persevere with Sooryavanshi. He'll be a tremendous asset for India,” he said.With the 2027 ODI World Cup on the horizon, Engineer believes Sooryavanshi's fearless approach and match-winning ability make him a player India should invest in now rather than wait for the future.
Article Summary: Farokh Engineer believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already done enough to earn an ODI call-up. Engineer wants the 15-year-old to open alongside Rohit Sharma ahead of the 2027 World Cup. The former India star feels Shubman Gill should be moved to No. 4.

Article Title: From England disappointment to Zimbabwe success: India coach hails Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 'maturity level'
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

India's interim head coach VVS Laxman said 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has shown remarkable growth in his understanding of the game over the last six months, adding that the teenager's maturity has helped him handle pressure at the international level.Sooryavanshi finished India's tour of Zimbabwe on a high, winning both the Player of the Match and Player of the Series awards after India completed a 3-0 sweep with a 35-run win in the third and final T20I on Sunday."What is really impressive is the way he's evolved as a person. The maturity level, the understanding, and the awareness over the last six months has actually skyrocketed. And that's why he's been able to handle tough situations," Laxman said during the post-match press conference.The left-hander scored 151 runs in three innings at an average of 50.33, including 81 in the final match, which laid the platform for India's victory.His performances came after a difficult debut series against England, where he managed scores of 13, 14 and 15 before being dropped for the fifth and final T20I as India lost the series 0-4."He played Under-19 World Cup and in a matter of four to five months, he dominated the IPL.We know how tough IPL competition can be."Taking on the best of bowlers from not only India but around the world, the way he evolved, the way he progressed as an international cricketer and he showed what kind of potential and class and talent he has," said Laxman, who is serving as the interim head coach while Gautam Gambhir is on a break before India's two-Test tour of Sri Lanka next month.Laxman also highlighted Sooryavanshi's desire to improve, recalling how the youngster wanted to stay on the field despite suffering an injury during the final T20I."We have to also remember that he's just 15 years old. He's a very young boy. And he himself wants to get better in every aspect of the game. And if you see it, even today's game, he was taking the hot spot."Even though he got injured, he still wanted to be on the field. But it was our physio who actually asked him to come out. So, that's the eagerness and the earnestness he has to do and contribute in every possible way to the team," said Laxman.When asked if he expected Sooryavanshi to recover so strongly after his difficult start in England, Laxman said he was not surprised because the youngster had already shown he could deal with pressure during the IPL."It (performance) was on expected lines. Again, last year when he played for Rajasthan Royals for the first time, I think the way he handled pressure, because I believe that any IPL match is equivalent to an international match."And at the age of 14 or 15, when you're playing an IPL match, either you can be overawed by the big occasion or absorb and embrace the pressure. And I think he's taken the second option where he embraced the pressure. So, I'm not at all surprised the way this series has gone," said Laxman.
Article Summary: India's interim head coach VVS Laxman says 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has shown remarkable growth in his understanding of the game over the last six months. The left-hander scored 151 runs in three innings at an average of 50.33, including 81 in the final match, which laid the platform for India's victory. India completed a 3-0 sweep with a 35-run win in the third and final T20I.

Article Title: 'Thank you VVS sir': Shreyas Iyer credits Laxman after India's 3-0 Zimbabwe sweep
Article Text:
VVS Laxman and Shreyas Iyer (Screengrab)

India's comprehensive 3-0 T20I series victory over Zimbabwe ended with mutual appreciation between captain Shreyas Iyer and stand-in head coach VVS Laxman , as both credited each other's leadership for the team's commanding performances.A relatively inexperienced Indian squad, missing several first-choice players including Sanju Samson , Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana, completed the clean sweep with a 35-run victory in the third and final T20I in Harare on Sunday.In a dressing room video shared by the BCCI after the series, Laxman singled out Iyer for praise, applauding the skipper's attitude and leadership despite a difficult beginning to his tenure as India's T20I captain."I would like to specially congratulate Shreyas because he had a rough start to his captaincy career but the way he came back, right from the first day when he joined us one day before the first game, he was very optimistic," Laxman said, referring to India's 0-4 series defeat against England earlier this month.Laxman said Iyer's confidence was evident from the outset, even though the squad featured several fresh faces with only a handful of players carrying over from the England tour."It's a new group of players. We know that only four or five of those who were there in England joined us on this tour. But he was so confident and a lot of credit for this victory should be given to the captain, the way he encouraged each one of you," he added.Iyer, who registered his first series win as India's T20I captain, returned the compliment by thanking Laxman for the influence he had on the squad throughout the tour."I think we were flawless, honestly speaking, throughout the series barring the catches that we dropped. It was a phenomenal effort by everyone in the team, including the support staff.""Thank you VVS sir for motivating us and inspiring us. Each and every day when we stepped onto the field, I think everything that you mentioned was apt and we could relate to it. So, thank you so much," Iyer said.Laxman stepped in as interim head coach for the Zimbabwe series while regular head coach Gautam Gambhir took a break following India's demanding tour of the UK. Gambhir is expected to return for India's Test tour of Sri Lanka in August.The successful Zimbabwe campaign once again highlighted Laxman's ability to guide young squads on short assignments, while Iyer's composed leadership helped India bounce back strongly after the disappointing England series earlier in the month.

Article Title: Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and priceless lessons: Abhishek Moond and Vasudev Prasad Singh soak in Australia's fast-bowling culture
Article Text:

(I can't believe I have marked my run-up alongside Hazlewood and Starc)," Ashok Kumar recalled the first conversation he had with his ward, Vasudev Prasad Singh, from Brisbane on July 14.Singh, 20, from Bihar's Muzaffarpur district, and 18-year-old Abhishek Moond from Rajasthan's Sikar district trained alongside Australia's Test squad for two weeks as part of the long-running partnership between the MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia.MRF Pace Foundation Program Manager and Head Coach M. Senthilnathan said watching the two youngsters during the first couple of days was an absolute delight."They were like kids in a candy store, pinching each other. They were overwhelmed for the first two days," Senthilnathan told TimesofIndia.com from Brisbane."Vasu hails from Bihar and Abhishek from Rajasthan. They come from smaller cities in our country. To train with Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood is something they would not have imagined even in their wildest dreams. But having said that, it was a great learning curve for them.They rubbed shoulders with two of the world's best. They saw how they train, how they bowl in the nets and, most importantly, how they understand and manage their bodies, which is very important for every fast bowler," he added.The duo trained from July 13 to July 24 at Cricket Australia's National Cricket Centre (NCC) in Brisbane. They also attended training sessions involving the Australian men's Test squad at the Allan Border Field."Getting the opportunity to train with the Australian senior team has been an incredible experience," Moond told this website."The whole environment is different. The batters are of the highest quality, so you have to be consistent and keep bowling in the right areas. I've learned that I need to pitch the ball slightly fuller than my usual back-of-a-length."The bounce and movement have been excellent, and the experience has been fantastic. Training with players of this calibre is a huge confidence booster. At my age, getting the chance to practise alongside cricketers I've watched since childhood is very special. I'm sure I'll learn a lot from them."Like Moond, Vasudev Prasad Singh believes the experience extends far beyond simply sharing the nets with Australia's Test stars. For him, the opportunity is about learning the finer aspects of fast bowling in conditions that reward pace and discipline."The biggest advantage of this tour is the opportunity to train with the Australian senior team. We get to learn so much from them. The environment here is excellent, and the conditions are ideal for fast bowling," said Vasudev Prasad Singh."We're able to bowl long spells, which helps us improve our skills. Exposure like this is extremely important for a cricketer. Bowling to world-class batters in favourable conditions teaches you where to bowl, how to plan your spells and how to set the field."Ashok Kumar, a former Bihar cricketer who has worked with the likes of Sakib Hussain and Mohammad Izhar, two other promising pacers from the state, shared an interesting story about his ward."For someone who has bowled most of his formative years on matting wickets, this was an experience he will never forget. Vasu has represented Bihar at the Under-19 and Under-23 levels and has all the attributes to play for India. He has a very good outswing. He is still raw but will be a ready product in a couple of years," Ashok said.Senthilnathan echoed Kumar's sentiments."They are good boys. Their work ethic is excellent. They train hard. They are still raw, but they will only get better from here," he said.The visit is part of a high-performance exchange program that has connected Indian and Australian cricket for more than three decades, making it one of the sport's longest-running international development partnerships.The MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia have worked together since 1992, building on Australian pace legend Dennis Lillee's association with the Foundation after it was established in Chennai in 1987.The program gives young Indian cricketers exposure to Australian conditions and training methods, while Australian players sharpen their skills in subcontinental conditions. The partnership has helped shape several leading fast bowlers. Australian greats Glenn McGrath, Mitchell Johnson and Brett Lee have all been associated with the Foundation, while Indian stars such as Javagal Srinath and Zaheer Khan are among those who benefited from its development pathway.Looking ahead, Senthilnathan believes the Brisbane stint will prove to be a defining chapter in the youngsters' development."We've had a long association with Cricket Australia and it has helped so many Indian pacers over the years. We saw what Prafull Hinje and Sakib Hussain did after their exposure here. Prafull spent three weeks training in Brisbane and returned a different bowler. Experiences like these accelerate growth. Vasu and Abhishek are still raw, but they have the attitude and work ethic to go a long way. You'll see them making an impact in the years to come," he said.
Article Summary: Vasudev Prasad Singh and Abhishek Moond trained alongside Australia's Test squad for two weeks as part of the long-running partnership between the MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia. The duo trained from July 13 to July 24 at Cricket Australia's National Cricket Centre in Brisbane.

India completed a 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi dominating the headlines after the 15-year-old became the youngest player ever to win the Player of the Series award in men's international cricket.Sooryavanshi announced himself with a blistering 50 off just 18 balls in the first T20I, followed it up with 20 off nine deliveries in the second match, and capped off the series with a superb 81 off 49 balls in the third and final T20I.However, the success Sooryavanshi enjoyed was in stark contrast to that of his opening partner, Abhishek Sharma . NEW DELHI: Pakistan ended Day 2 of the first Test against West Indies in a strong position, reaching 199/3 in reply to the hosts' first-innings total of 311.Former captain Shan Masood led the fightback with an unbeaten 88, making an impressive return with the bat after recently stepping down from the captaincy. He was well supported by Imam-ul-Haq, who scored 63 as the pair shared a crucial 155-run partnership.Pakistan lost an early wicket when Azan Awais was bowled by Kemar Roach , but Masood and Imam steadied the innings with positive strokeplay.Masood brought up his half-century in just 46 balls, while Imam reached his 11th Test fifty before being dismissed for 63. New captain Babar Azam added 23 before falling late in the day, while Salman Agha remained unbeaten at stumps alongside Masood after bad light brought play to an early close.Earlier, West Indies were bowled out for 311 after resuming the day at 194/3. Shai Hope top-scored with 92, narrowly missing out on a century, while Kavem Hodge made 84.Hope anchored the innings despite losing partners regularly and received useful contributions from Shamar Joseph, who scored a quick 23.Pakistan's bowlers pulled things back after West Indies' solid start. Mohammad Ali picked up four wickets, while Mohammad Abbas claimed three after making an immediate impact with the second new ball.Khurram Shahzad also struck early to remove Hodge, helping Pakistan wrap up the innings before their batters took control through Masood and Imam.
Article Summary: Pakistan reach 199/3 at stumps on Day 2 of the first Test against West Indies. Shan Masood top scored with 88, while Imam-ul-Haq scored 63. West Indies were bowled out for 311 after resuming the day at 194/3.

Article Title: Yash Dayal set to join Chhattisgarh, seeks NOC from UPCA
Article Text:
Royal Challengers Bengaluru's Yash Dayal (PTI Photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of Yash Dayal's cricket career do you find most impressive? His comeback and resilience His consistent performances 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh pacer Yash Dayal has sought a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) to switch to Chhattisgarh for the upcoming domestic season.Speculation was rife that Dayal would feature in the UPT20 League after playing in the Ghaziabad Premier League in June, where he took nine wickets in four matches. However, the left-arm pacer has decided to move on.Yash represented Uttar Pradesh from 2018 to 2025, playing 27 first-class matches and taking 84 wickets. In List A cricket, he claimed 36 wickets in 23 matches, while in T20s, he picked up 66 wickets in 71 matches.Talking to TOI, Dayal said, "I have applied to the UPCA for an NOC. From next month, I will join the Chhattisgarh team's fitness camp and play for Chhattisgarh in the upcoming domestic season."The left-arm pacer revealed that talks with the Chhattisgarh Cricket Association had been underway even before the start of the season, but he initially needed time to make a decision. After discussions with his seniors and family, he decided to go ahead with the move.Dayal said leaving Uttar Pradesh was an emotional and difficult decision, as the UPCA had played a major role in his career."Playing for the UP team and representing Uttar Pradesh in the Ranji Trophy has been extremely special and a matter of pride for me. The UP Cricket Association is very close to my heart. UP gave me recognition. I played in the IPL and was also selected for the Indian team. The UPCA has contributed immensely to whatever I have achieved," he said.Speaking about the difficult phase he has faced recently, including legal and mental challenges, Dayal said cricket helped him stay strong and focus on making a comeback."As a cricketer, no one wants to go through a phase that shakes his life. But cricket has taught me how to make a comeback and perform in every situation. I did not run away from difficulties. My family and my coaches always stood by me," he said."Many times I felt like giving up because, despite being capable, I was not able to play. In such circumstances, sometimes the mind starts to break," he added.The pacer also clarified his situation with Royal Challengers Bengaluru, saying the franchise had not dropped him. He said he remained part of the squad but was not travelling with the team during the season.On the ongoing legal matters, Dayal confirmed that he had been granted bail in both cases and that the proceedings were still underway. "In both cases, I have officially been granted bail and the cases are still under process," he said.Meanwhile, a senior UPCA official told TOI, "Yash has applied for an NOC, and his request is still under consideration."
Article Summary: Yash Dayal has sought a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) to switch to Chhattisgarh. The left-arm pacer represented Uttar Pradesh from 2018 to 2025, playing 27 first-class matches and taking 84 wickets.

Article Title: 'Why different rules for different players?' - Abhishek Sharma's poor form sparks Sanju Samson debate
Article Text:
India's Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson (ANI Photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view Who should get more opportunities in India's T20I team? Players with current form Players with proven performances 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Hanuma Vihari has questioned Team India's decision to continue backing Abhishek Sharma despite his poor run of form in the ongoing T20I series against Zimbabwe. The former India batter believes the selectors have applied different standards to Abhishek and Sanju Samson, especially after Samson lost his place despite performing well in major tournaments.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Vihari pointed out that Samson was dropped after a few poor games before the T20 World Cup but returned strongly to become one of India's standout performers.He said, "Before the World Cup, Sanju Samson did not perform in five games and lost his spot in the starting 11. He then made a comeback and became Player of the Tournament. In that same tournament, how many runs did Abhishek Sharma make?"He also highlighted Abhishek's recent numbers, saying, "In the UK series, apart from one fifty, there were no scores at all. Not even 20s and 30s, no significant score. One fifty in the last eight matches. If you include the World Cup, three half-centuries in the last 18 matches."Vihari argued that Samson proved himself when it mattered by scoring three consecutive fifties during India's T20 World Cup-winning campaign, but still lost his place in the side as youngster Vaibhav Sooryavanshi emerged as a preferred option.Questioning the selection policy, he said, "How many matches Samson played in the World Cup? Three. And fifties in all three. Abhishek's highest score in the five matches is 16. Why is no one talking about it? When it comes to Samson, they say he is inconsistent. Fair enough.
