Article Summary: Hanuma Vihari questions Team India's decision to continue backing Abhishek Sharma. Former India batter believes the selectors have applied different standards to the two players. Samson was dropped after a few poor games before the T20 World Cup but returned strongly to become a standout performer.

Article Title: As father fights blood cancer, Rishikanta bags CWG silver
Article Text:
Rishikanta Singh Chanambam (right) with his family in Imphal and (pic right) after winning silver in Glasgow on Sunday.

TOI

As Rishikanta Singh Chanambam stepped onto the platform for the men’s 60kg weightlifting competition at Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Sunday, his biggest supporters gathered around a mobile phone over 7,000km away in Uttarlai, Barmer, Rajasthan.Although Rishikanta hails from Ngairangbam Makha Maning Leikai in Manipur ’s Imphal West district, his parents have been living with his elder brother, Amarjit Singh , in Rajasthan for the past few months. His father is undergoing treatment for blood cancer at AIIMS Jodhpur, where he has already completed three rounds of chemotherapy and is responding well.Even as Rishikanta lifted a combined 264kg to claim the silver medal, thoughts of his father were never far from his mind.“We have had a very difficult life, and I’ve always tried to make him smile because I never got to spend much time with him,” Rishikanta said during an exclusive interaction with. “The last time I went home, I even took him to a scooter showroom so he could finally buy one for himself.”Looking after his family, however, has been a priority for Rishikanta since childhood.“I used to work as a daily-wage labourer with some of my friends,” the 28-year-old recalled.“I worked for about two to three months. I wasn’t a skilled worker, so I mostly helped with whatever work was available and earned around ₹150 a day.”He initially took up the work to earn enough money to study in a private school like many of his friends. But as the family’s financial struggles deepened, the money he earned also went towards supporting the household.While both his parents worked as daily-wage labourers on other people’s farms, his father also worked as a taxi driver to supplement the family’s income. Even then, they struggled to provide for a family of six — the parents, two sons and two daughters.“We don’t even own farmland,” said Amarjit, who has been serving in the Indian Air Force since 2012. “Our parents worked on other people’s fields to earn a living.”The family’s fortunes began to change only after Amarjit secured a job. Until then, every rupee mattered, and Rishikanta’s dream often depended on his elder brother’s support. “My elder brother is like my second father,” Rishikanta said. “There was a time when I had no income. He paid for my training and competitions. Whatever I am today is because of him.”Amarjit never thought twice before helping, and today he could not be prouder of what his younger brother has achieved.As for Rishikanta’s sporting journey, it began after a veteran coach persuaded the family to send him for trials at National Sports Academy in Imphal. He earned selection and spent his formative years there under Brojendro Singh before progressing through the Sports Authority of India’s (SAI) system.The road, however, was anything but smooth. After ageing out of the academy, he was forced to stay at home for several months without training before coaches and officials helped him resume his career at SAI National Centre of Excellence. He later joined Indian Navy in 2019, which provided him with financial security before breaking into the national camp. Over the past two years, he has trained under chief national coach Vijay Sharma in Modinagar.Ironically, weightlifting wasn’t Rishikanta’s first love.“My dream was to become a boxer,” he said. “I even trained in boxing for a while because I admired the sport after watching Dingko Singh. But once I started competing in weightlifting and won a tournament, I realised this was where I belonged.”That decision transformed his life.Having narrowly missed out on a medal at the previous Commonwealth Games, Rishikanta looked set to crown his journey with gold in Glasgow after setting a CWG record of 121kg in the snatch. But a lingering knee injury, which had troubled him for weeks leading up to the competition, limited him in the clean and jerk, leaving him with silver. The medal, however, made him the first male weightlifter from Manipur to stand on the Commonwealth Games podium.“I believe I could have won gold if I had been fully fit,” Rishikanta admitted. “The injury didn’t allow me to train the way I wanted before the competition.”For Rishikanta, however, the silver represented far more than a medal. It was a tribute to parents who spent years working as labourers to keep the family afloat, an elder brother he still calls his “second father”, and the promise of a young boy who once earned ₹150 a day as a labourer that he would one day make all their sacrifices worthwhile.
Article Summary: Rishikanta Singh Chanambam won silver in the men’s 60kg weightlifting competition at Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Sunday. The 28-year-old hails from Ngairangbam Makha Maning Leikai in Manipur ’s Imphal West district. His parents have been living with his elder brother, Amarjit Singh, in Rajasthan for the past few months.

Article Title: India's artistic gymnasts return empty-handed after disappointing Glasgow campaign
Article Text:
India's Protistha Samanta (AP Photo/Kin Cheung)

New Delhi: India's artistic gymnasts will return empty-handed from Glasgow after a disappointing campaign that exposed shortcomings in preparation, fitness management and administration.Protistha Samanta's seventh-place finish in Monday's women's vault final was the contingent's best result.India's biggest medal hope, Pranati Nayak, competed despite carrying a Grade II ankle ligament tear, according to coach Ashok Mishra. She was nevertheless cleared to compete despite not being fully fit and struggled throughout. Pranati finished 11th in the vault qualification.Eshitaa Rewale (15th) and Nishka Agarwal (19th) also failed to progress in the vault, while Samanta (27th) and Rewale (28th) missed out on the all-around final. India finished ninth in the women's team event, while the men's team fared no better, ending seventh.The disappointing returns should ring alarm bells for the authorities. National coach Manoj Rana said the campaign had suffered because of inadequate planning."The absence of individualised performance planning and athlete-specific support limited the team's ability to maximise its competitive potential," he said, calling for long-term athlete management, better technical support and coordinated performance planning."Elite gymnastics requires tailored preparation, including event-specific strategy, technical analysis, physical conditioning, recovery management and psychological support. A more structured approach could have enhanced performance and improved medal prospects," he added.Questions also remain over athlete welfare. Despite persistent injury concerns, Pranati travelled without a physiotherapist. The Gymnastics Federation of India reportedly declined requests for one and did not propose a physio for the contingent.The federation's prolonged internal feud, delayed elections and governance issues have further hurt the sport. With the Asian Games looming, India's underwhelming display in Glasgow should serve as a wake-up call for the authorities.
Article Summary: India's artistic gymnasts will return empty-handed from Glasgow. India's biggest medal hope, Pranati Nayak, competed despite carrying a Grade II ankle ligament tear. India finished ninth in the women's team event, while the men's team fared no better.

Article Title: Daily wage labourers' son Muthupandi Raja overcomes setbacks to win Commonwealth Games silver
Article Text:
Muthupandi Raja (ANI Photo)

Chennai: The silver medal that Tamil Nadu weightlifter Muthupandi Raja won on Sunday probably belonged as much to his parents as it did to him. Their years of back-breaking work as daily wage labourers gave their son the chance to chase a dream that found its defining moment in Glasgow.The medal was the culmination of a journey that nearly came to an abrupt end. Injuries and health setbacks made Raja contemplate quitting the sport, but his family and coaches stood firmly behind him.He suffered an injury during the 2019 Commonwealth Weightlifting Championships and underwent surgery, keeping him out of action for nearly two years. In 2022, he was diagnosed with jaundice and later underwent an appendicitis surgery, which sidelined him for almost another year. It was during this difficult phase that he thought of quitting the sport.However, the enforced break helped him complete a course in strength and conditioning, besides learning about sports science, which taught him how to deal with injuries.Raja's elder brother, Suresh, who was also a national-level weightlifter, told TOI that this was "just the beginning"."This silver should be an inspiration for Raja and we want to see him compete at the Olympics," Suresh told TOI.For Raja, it all began in a small gym in Sankaralingapuram village in Thoothukudi district, where he trained alongside Suresh. Seeing the brothers' physique, local coaches persuaded them to take up weightlifting. Raja's talent quickly shone through, earning him a place at the Sports Authority of India (SAI) training centre in Mayiladuthurai within a year.But the brothers' journeys eventually took different paths. Suresh was forced to quit the sport three years ago due to financial constraints."Seeing my brother win a medal in Glasgow feels like winning the medal myself. What I could not achieve, he has done. The struggles have finally paid off," said Suresh, who now does odd jobs."We did not know anything about weightlifting initially as we had gone to the gym for strength training. When we asked our parents if we could pursue weightlifting, they told us to do what we liked and supported us wholeheartedly. My father bought us whatever we needed by taking loans from villagers, and the people in our village were equally supportive."
Article Summary: Muthupandi Raja won a silver medal at the Commonwealth Weightlifting Championships in Glasgow. The medal was the culmination of a journey that nearly came to an abrupt end. Injuries and health setbacks made Raja contemplate quitting the sport, but his family and coaches stood firmly behind him.

Article Title: Gurindervir Singh fails to reach 100m semifinals despite 'fastest Indian' tag
Article Text:
India's Gurindervir Singh (PTI Photo)

Tags raise expectations. The tag of 'fastest Indian' had helped hype Gurindervir Singh's debut at the Commonwealth Games. In the end, he did not even make the cut for the semifinals.The Punjab sprinter, who became the first Indian to complete the 100m in 10.09 seconds at the Federation Cup in May, could manage only 10.39 seconds to finish 28th overall in the heats.Although he was the second fastest in his heat behind Jamaica's Rohan Watson (10.13s), Gurindervir failed to make the top 17 fastest athletes who qualified for the semifinals. At the Olympics and the World Championships, qualification for the next round is decided by a combination of the top three finishers from each heat and the next fastest athletes overall.The sprinter described his performance as "unsatisfactory" but insisted he had given his best despite not being at 100 per cent."I wasn't feeling 100 per cent before my race. I had a small hamstring injury after the Fed Cup in Ranchi. That is why I had to skip the inter-state and Taiwan meets before the CWG," Gurindervir told TOI."But I had worked on my injury and was fit before the CWG. However, today I think it wasn't my day.I still tried to give my best in the race, but it wasn't enough," he added.Asked whether he had been under pressure during his Commonwealth Games debut, the 25-year-old dismissed the suggestion."I don't think I had any pressure, be it of my CWG debut or keeping up with the tag of a national record holder. Like success, failures are also part of an athlete's life, so I would put this behind me and work on improving my performance in the next meets and at the Asian Games, if I qualify," Gurindervir said.Gurindervir's coach, Sarabjit Singh, who trains him in Jalandhar, believed the attention surrounding his athlete ahead of the Commonwealth Games may have had an impact."He may not realise it now, but I feel such hype puts some pressure on the subconscious mind," he said."Expectations were raised after he became the first Indian to run a sub-10.10s race. He was everywhere. Also, there was hardly any gap between the national record performance and the CWG for him to settle down. Nonetheless, I am sure he will take this as a lesson and work harder for the future."
Article Summary: Gurindervir Singh fails to qualify for semifinals of 100m at Commonwealth Games. Punjab sprinter became first Indian to complete 100m in 10.09 seconds at Federation Cup. Gurindervirs coach Sarabjit Singh believes hype surrounding his athlete may have had impact.

Article Title: India add three more weightlifting medals; Tejas Shirse ends 60-year Commonwealth Games wait
Article Text:
Glasgow: India's Tejas Shirse, second left, Saint Lucia's Khailan Vitalis, left, and others compete in the men's 110m hurdles round 1 (PTI Photo)

Indian weightlifters are quite literally carrying the weight of expectations in Glasgow. After Mirabai Chanu's gold and Rishikanta Singh's silver, Muthupandi Raja, Gyaneshwari Yadav and Bindyarani Devi added two silvers and a bronze to take India's weightlifting haul to five medals.Gyaneshwari, 23, lifted a total of 199kg after an absorbing duel with Nigeria's Onome Omolola Didih, who won gold with a Games-record total of 206kg. Canada's Rebeka Groulx took bronze with 178kg.A confident Gyaneshwari progressed steadily through both disciplines. She opened with 82kg in the snatch before successfully lifting 85kg and 88kg in her next two attempts.She also increased the weight with each attempt in the clean and jerk, successfully lifting 103kg, 107kg and 111kg. However, Didih, who had lifted 93kg in the snatch, maintained her lead with clean and jerk lifts of 105kg, 110kg and 113kg.Later on Monday, Bindyarani lifted a total of 199kg to win bronze in the women's 58kg category. The 27-year-old from Manipur registered 87kg in the snatch and 112kg in the clean and jerk.Bindyarani completed all three snatch attempts, lifting 83kg, 85kg and 87kg. In the clean and jerk, she failed at 110kg in her opening attempt but boldly raised the weight to 112kg and completed the lift.She then failed at 116kg in her final attempt.Even a successful 116kg lift would not have changed the colour of her medal, as it would have taken her total only to 203kg. Canada's Ann-Sophie Taschereau won silver with 215kg, while Nigeria's Rafiatu Folashade Lawal claimed gold with a Games-record total of 229kg.Earlier, Raja, 26, secured silver in the men's 65kg event with a total of 286kg late on Sunday night. He lifted 126kg in the snatch and 160kg in the clean and jerk to finish behind Malaysia's Muhamad Aznil bin Bidin, who won gold with a Games-record total of 299kg. Papua New Guinea's Morea Baru took bronze with 282kg.It was also an encouraging day in athletics for India, with Tejas Shirse qualifying for the men's 110m hurdles final. The national record-holder became the first Indian in 60 years to reach the Commonwealth Games final in the men's sprint hurdles. Gurbachan Singh Randhawa was the last to do so, finishing seventh in the equivalent 120-yard hurdles at the 1966 Games in Kingston, Jamaica.The Maharashtra athlete clocked 13.76 seconds to finish sixth overall and third in Heat 1.In the long jump, M Sreeshankar and Lokesh Sathyanathan qualified for the men's final. Sreeshankar jumped 8.01m on his opening attempt to clear the automatic qualifying standard of 8.00m. Lokesh finished fourth in Group B with an opening jump of 7.77m and advanced as one of the 12 best performers.Indian boxer Sachin Siwach stormed into the quarterfinals of the men's 60kg event after defeating England's William Hewitt by a 4-1 points decision in the round of 16 on Monday. In the men's 80kg category, Ankush Panghal dominated Antigua and Barbuda's Zalaan Jan to register a unanimous 5-0 victory and reach the quarterfinals.
Article Summary: Muthupandi Raja, Gyaneshwari Yadav and Bindyarani Devi added two silvers and a bronze to take India's weightlifting haul to five medals. Tejas Shirse became the first Indian in 60 years to reach the men's 110m hurdles final in the Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: CWG 2026 Day 5: Sharmila Dhankar claims India's first-ever para-athletics gold, headlines six-medal haul
Article Text:
Sharmila Dhankar

Weightlifters keep medal rush alive

Boxers progress, mixed fortunes elsewhere

NEW DELHI: India on Monday enjoyed one of its best days at the Commonwealth Games with six medals overall, with Sharmila Dhankar making history after becoming the country's first-ever para-athletics gold medallist.On Day 5 of the event, she won the women's F57 shot put title with a season-best throw of 9.81m, ending India's 20-year wait for a para-athletics medal at the Games.The F57 category is for athletes with lower limb impairments, limb deficiencies or reduced muscle power.Shilpa K. Shyla clinched a bronze in the women’s shot put F57 event.The celebrations continued in athletics with Sarvesh Kushare becoming the first Indian to win a silver medal in the men's high jump. The national record holder cleared 2.25m and narrowly missed the gold on countback after tying with Jamaica's Romaine Beckford.Adarsh Ram finished fifth, while Tejaswin Shankar withdrew early as a precaution before the decathlon.Weightlifting once again delivered for India. Valluri Ajaya Babu won silver in the men's 79kg event after finishing just one kilogram behind Malaysia's Erry Hidayat Muhammad in a thrilling contest.Gyaneshwari Yadav also claimed silver in the women's 53kg category with career-best lifts, while Bindyarani Devi added a bronze in the 58kg class, taking India's weightlifting medal tally to six.Indian boxing also had a productive day as Sachin Siwach, Ankush and Sakshi Chaudhary advanced to the quarterfinals with convincing wins, although Sumit exited after a narrow defeat.There were disappointments too. Sprinter Gurindervir Singh failed to qualify for the 100m semifinals, while hurdler Tejas Shirse finished last in the 110m hurdles final after competing with an injury."In the warm up, I suffered a Navicular stress fracture in my left leg. I didn't want to pull out so I told my physio to tape it," Shirse told news agency PTI."I am the first Indian to qualify for the 110m hurdles final in the CWG, so I didn't want to let the whole nation down (by pulling out)," he added.Swimming also brought little success, with Sajan Prakash, Aryan Nehra and para-swimmer Swatik Patil finishing outside the medals.
Article Summary: Sharmila Dhankar becomes the country's first-ever para-athletics gold medallist. Sarvesh Kushare becomes the first Indian to win a silver medal in the men's high jump. Valluri Ajaya Babu wins silver in men's 79kg event.

Article Title: Commonwealth Games: Gyaneshwari Yadav wins silver as India claims fourth weightlifting medal
Article Text:
Gyaneshwari Yadav during the women's weightlifting 53kg Snatch during day four of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, Monday, July 27, 2026. (AP)

The standings after snatch:

Didih: 93kg

Gyaneshwari: 88kg

Groulx: 83kg

India's weightlifting contingent added another Commonwealth Games medal on Sunday as Gyaneshwari Yadav clinched silver in the women's 53kg final.It was India's fourth weightlifting medal at the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Earlier, Mirabai Chanu (women's 48kg - gold), Rishikanta Singh (men's 60kg - silver) and Muthupandi Raja (men's 65kg - silver) had also finished on the podium in their respective categories.Weightlifting comprises two disciplines — the snatch and the clean and jerk — with each lifter getting three attempts in both.In the snatch, athletes lift the barbell from the ground to overhead in one continuous movement with a wide grip. In the clean and jerk, they first lift the bar to their shoulders (clean), pause, and then drive it overhead (jerk), holding it steady until the buzzer.Gyaneshwari lifted 88kg in the snatch to finish second. Nigeria's Onome Didih led the field with 93kg, while Canada's Groulx was third with 83kg.In the clean and jerk, Gyaneshwari successfully lifted 111kg. However, Didih managed 113kg to retain her lead and secure the gold medal, leaving the Indian lifter with silver.The 23-year-old from Bhondiya village in Chhattisgarh totalled 199kg (88kg snatch + 111kg clean and jerk) but Nigeria's Onome Omolola Didih stole the show with a stunning 206kg (93kg + 113kg), rewriting both the Commonwealth and Commonwealth Games records to take the gold.It is the fourth weightlifting medal for India at the CWG and fifth medal overall.
Article Summary: Gyaneshwari Yadav won silver in the women's 53kg final. It is India's fourth weightlifting medal at the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Nigeria's Onome Omolola Didih stole the show with a stunning 206kg.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Gurindervir Singh fails to qualify for Men's 100m semifinals
Article Text:
Glasgow: India's Gurindervir Singh competes in the men's 100m round 1 heat 4 athletics at the 23rd Commonwealth Games, in Glasgow, Scotland. (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)

Promising start but faded in final metres



National record holder unable to repeat best form

Azamati, Saminu lead qualifiers



India's Gurindervir Singh suffered an early exit from the Commonwealth Games 2026 after failing to qualify for the men's 100m semifinals. The 25-year-old clocked 10.39 seconds in his heat, finishing 28th overall, with only the top 17 athletes progressing to the next round. Arriving in Glasgow with hopes of becoming the first Indian to break the elusive 10-second barrier on the international stage, Gurindervir was unable to produce his best performance when it mattered most.Competing from lane five in Heat 4, the Punjab sprinter made a promising start and stayed alongside Jamaica's Rohan Watson through the opening stages. However, he faded over the final 30-35 metres as Watson surged ahead to win the heat in 10.13 seconds. Although Gurindervir finished second in his heat, his time was not enough to secure a semifinal berth. Watson progressed after finishing ninth overall.A total of 17 athletes advanced from the opening round, while seven sprinters had already received automatic byes into the semifinals. Despite benefiting from a legal 1.5 m/s tailwind, Gurindervir could not convert the favourable conditions into a faster time. His 10.39-second effort was well below his personal best and national record of 10.09 seconds, set at the Federation Cup in Ranchi earlier this year, where he became the first Indian to run under 10.10 seconds.Ghana's Benjamin Azamati and Abdul-Rasheed Saminu emerged as the fastest qualifiers from the heats, clocking 10.00 seconds and 10.01 seconds, respectively, to lead the field into the semifinals.
Article Summary: India's Gurindervir Singh failed to qualify for the men's 100m semifinals. The 25-year-old clocked 10.39 seconds in his heat, finishing 28th overall. Ghana's Benjamin Azamati and Abdul-Rasheed Saminu lead qualifiers.

Article Title: 'You were busy planting seeds of hate': FIFA backs Trump-Balogun decision, hits back at World Cup critics
Article Text:
Photo/Agencies

On Iran and US relations

Defending Balogun decision

One week after the FIFA World Cup final, FIFA president Gianni Infantino defended the tournament and criticised what he described as negative coverage, accusing some critics of “spreading hate and false rumors. ”In a 900-word statement published across a 15-page post on his Instagram account and on FIFA’s website late Sunday, Infantino said FIFA had succeeded in staging the World Cup and bringing people together.He praised FIFA for “delivering the best show in the world” and said the tournament had brought “joy and togetherness.”“Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all,” Infantino wrote, addressing his comments to “those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumors.”FIFA and Infantino faced criticism during the World Cup over several issues, including Iran team officials, a Somali referee and some fans being denied entry to the United States, allegations of political influence by US President Donald Trump in allowing Folarin Balogun to avoid a suspension after receiving a red card, high ticket prices and commercial breaks introduced midway through each half of all 104 matches.“Every city was packed with fans from all around the globe,” Infantino wrote.“While they celebrated, you were busy planting seeds of hate.”“While you hide, we are exploring the streets of Canada, Mexico, and the United States, talking with fans, engaging with people, and ensuring everyone’s safety.”Iran's participation in matches held in the United States had been one of the major issues before the tournament. The Iranian team eventually shifted its training camp from Tucson, Arizona, to Tijuana in Mexico before the competition.“Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict,” Infantino wrote. “While you spread hatred, we worked tirelessly to unite two countries at war.”Some supporters were unable to enter the United States, including Michel Nkuka Mboladinga, the well-known Congo supporter, who attended one match in Mexico after being denied a US visa.“You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world,” Infantino wrote. “Countries facing serious health issues or other challenges were granted visas.”Infantino also responded to criticism over the handling of US forward Folarin Balogun's red card.He said “subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine.”FIFA did not cancel Balogun's red card, which sometimes happens in domestic competitions. Instead, it deferred his one-match suspension for a probationary period. FIFA has not yet released the disciplinary judge's written decision.Ending his statement, Infantino urged critics to focus on football instead of criticism.
Article Summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino releases a statement defending the World Cup. He accuses some critics of “spreading hate and false rumors’ FIFA and Infanino faced criticism over several issues, including Iran team officials, a Somali referee and some fans being denied entry to the United States.

Article Title: Who is Bara Sapoko Ndiaye? Meet the 18-year-old Senegalese midfield prodigy who went from making his FIFA World Cup debut to becoming part of Bayern Munich’s long-term plans
Article Text:
Bara Sapoko Ndiaye represented Senegal at the 2026 FIFA World Cup after making four Bundesliga appearances for Bayern Munich during the 2025-26 season. (Image via Getty)

Who is Bara Sapoko Ndiaye and why does Bayern Munich want to sign him?

How did Bara Sapoko Ndiaye move from Gambinos Stars to Bayern Munich?

What did Bara Sapoko Ndiaye do during his Bayern Munich loan?

Why did Senegal select Bara Sapoko Ndiaye for the 2026 World Cup?

Where could Bara Sapoko Ndiaye fit in Bayern Munich’s midfield?

Bayern Munich appears ready to turn a six-month loan into a long-term commitment. Transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano reported that the club has agreed to sign 18-year-old Senegal midfielder Bara Sapoko Ndiaye permanently from Gambinos Stars. The reported contract would run through 2031.As of July 27, Bayern had not formally announced the move. Sporting director Christoph Freund, however, said he expected Ndiaye to begin the season with the German champions. The teenager arrived on loan in January, played four Bundesliga games and later made Senegal’s 2026 World Cup squad.Ndiaye is an 18-year-old midfielder from Mékhé, Senegal. He was born on Dec. 31, 2007, stands 5’11” and is right-footed. He has played across central midfield, with Bayern describing him as a central attacking midfielder. Other accounts have characterized him as a box-to-box or attacking midfielder.Romano reported that Bayern had reached an agreement with Gambinos Stars for a permanent transfer.“FC Bayern agree on deal to sign talent Bara Sapoko Ndiaye on a permanent move. 18-year-old Senegalese talent joins from Gambinos Stars on a deal until 2031.”Romano added that the remaining formal steps were being completed. An official announcement was expected the following week.A contract through 2031 would give Bayern several seasons to develop Ndiaye. The midfielder does not need to become an immediate starter for the move to make sense. The deal’s reported length suggests that the club views him as more than short-term squad depth.Freund offered another indication that the transfer was close.“The final details still need to be clarified, but I expect him to start the season with us. Bara will undergo performance tests on Monday and then join the training camp at Tegernsee,” Freund said, according to Bild, via iMiaSanMia.Ndiaye began his youth career in Senegal with Thiès and Senegal Elite Stars. He later joined Gambinos Stars in The Gambia.His route to Bayern was connected to an existing development partnership. Bayern Munich and Los Angeles FC announced in Sept. 2023 that their Red&Gold Football joint venture had partnered with Gambinos Stars to develop talent in West Africa.Ndiaye also had a trial with Swiss club Grasshopper in 2025. Bayern then brought him to Germany on loan in January 2026 for the remainder of the 2025-26 season.He had not made a senior league appearance for Gambinos Stars before the move. Within four months, Ndiaye had played in the Bundesliga, started twice and collected a league winner’s medal.That rise explains the attention surrounding the reported permanent deal. Ndiaye moved from a football academy in The Gambia to Bayern’s first team in a matter of months. He then reached the World Cup before turning 19.Ndiaye made his professional debut on April 11 in Bayern’s 5-0 road win over FC St. Pauli. He replaced Jamal Musiala during the second half.Eight days later, he came off the bench in a 4-2 home victory over VfB Stuttgart. Bayern secured the 2025-26 Bundesliga title in that match. Ndiaye replaced Raphaël Guerreiro in the 78th minute.He made his first start on April 25 during a 4-3 comeback win at Mainz 05. Ndiaye started again on May 2 in a 3-3 draw against FC Heidenheim.His loan spell ended with four Bundesliga appearances and two starts. The sample was small, but Bayern’s next decision provided more context. The club reportedly pursued a five-year agreement instead of allowing Ndiaye to return to Gambinos Stars after the loan.Bayern had trusted a teenager without previous senior league experience during a title-winning season. That decision did not make him a guaranteed future starter. It did show that the coaching staff considered him ready for first-team minutes.Senegal coach Pape Thiaw named Ndiaye in the preliminary World Cup squad in May. The midfielder then made the final 26-player group.Ndiaye made his World Cup debut as an extra-time substitute against Belgium in the Round of 32. Senegal lost 3-2. The appearance gave him his second senior international cap.His selection came after only four Bundesliga matches. That timeline shows how quickly his standing changed during the first half of 2026. Senegal considered him ready for a World Cup squad, while Bayern began working on a permanent transfer.Senegalese outlet OnzeD’Afrik described Ndiaye as a midfielder with stamina, tactical intelligence and the ability to advance with the ball. That profile helps explain why Bayern used him in central midfield despite his limited senior experience.It also gives the club several options. Ndiaye can operate deeper in midfield or move forward when Bayern need another runner through the center.Ndiaye is unlikely to walk directly into Bayern’s starting lineup. Joshua Kimmich , Aleksandar Pavlović and Tom Bischof are among the club’s central midfield options.That depth could allow Bayern to manage his minutes without rushing his development. Ndiaye can train with the senior squad while the club decides where he will receive regular competitive opportunities.Those minutes could come with the first team, Bayern Munich II or through another development route. Bayern has not publicly confirmed a plan.The reported deal still requires an official announcement. Until that happens, Ndiaye remains a reported permanent signing rather than a confirmed Bayern player.Six months still changed his career. Ndiaye arrived without a senior league appearance, earned Bundesliga minutes, won a title and reached the World Cup. Bayern reportedly saw enough during that run to keep him until 2031.The contract would answer one question about his future. The bigger one is how quickly Ndiaye can turn Bayern’s long-term investment into a regular role.
Article Summary: Bayern Munich appears ready to turn a six-month loan into a long-term commitment. Transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano reported that the club has agreed to sign 18-year-old Senegal midfielder Bara Sapoko Ndiaye permanently from Gambinos Stars. The reported contract would run through 2031.

Article Title: Did Lionel Messi really give every Argentina player a gold Stanley set after losing the World Cup? Here’s the truth behind the viral gift
Article Text:
Kelci-Rose Bowers showed the personalized mate collection Lionel Messi gave Marcos Senesi after Argentina’s 2026 World Cup campaign. (Image via Getty)

Lionel Messi gave Argentina players personalized mate sets after the World Cup

The gift followed Argentina’s painful loss to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final

Lionel Messi left the 2026 World Cup without another title, but his Argentina teammates did not leave empty-handed.Kelci-Rose Bowers, the partner of Argentina defender Marcos Senesi, revealed that Messi gave every member of Lionel Scaloni’s squad a personalized mate set after the tournament. The collection included a custom bag, a gold-colored Stanley thermos, a mate cup, a metal straw and yerba mate. Multiple sources have reported details from Bowers’ social media video. So, yes, Messi did give every Argentina teammate a personalized Stanley set after the 2026 World Cup, but the bottles were gold-colored, not made of gold.Bowers showed Senesi’s gift in a video after Argentina’s campaign ended. The caramel-colored bag carried Senesi’s name, the Argentina crest, the World Cup logo and light blue details.“This is a personalised bag that Marcos got from the camp,” Bowers said. Inside the bag was a gold-colored Stanley thermos marked with Messi’s logo. The set also contained a mate cup, a bombilla straw and yerba mate, the dried leaves used to prepare the drink. Bowers said Messi gave the same type of set to every player in Argentina’s squad.“I have to show you guys something really cool. You will be very happy to see this. Marcos brought this bag from the camp.It also has his name written on it. This is his mate set. Messi gave this gift to all the players,” she said.Senesi then left the collection with Bowers for safekeeping. “Marcos gave me it to keep safe and take back to Miami,” she said.Bowers later described it as a “pretty cool gift” and said it was “pretty cool that I’ve got it.”The gift was personal because mate is part of Argentina’s daily team culture. Players regularly carry mate sets to training, hotels and stadiums. They prepare and share the drink together, so Messi selected something tied directly to the squad’s routine rather than a generic luxury item.The choice also matched Messi’s history of giving personalized gifts to Argentina teammates. After the 2022 World Cup, he reportedly commissioned 35 gold iPhones for players and staff. Reports at the time valued that collection at more than $200,000.Messi handed out the sets after Argentina fell short of winning consecutive World Cups. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final on July 19 at New York New Jersey Stadium. Ferran Torres scored the deciding goal in the 106th minute.Argentina had entered the final with a chance to become the first country since Brazil in 1962 to defend the World Cup. Messi could not score or assist in the loss, ending his run of 11 straight World Cup appearances with a goal contribution.Even so, the 39-year-old finished the tournament with eight goals and four assists in eight matches. Argentina reached another final four years after winning in Qatar, but Spain ended the repeat bid.Senesi joined Argentina’s squad late after Leonardo Balerdi suffered an injury. He made his World Cup debut in a 3-1 group-stage win over Jordan and later appeared again during the knockout rounds.The mate set now links Senesi’s first World Cup to Messi’s final act as captain during the tournament. It also showed how Messi responded after the defeat. He did not blame teammates or distance himself from the group. He gave every player the same personalized collection built around a shared Argentina tradition.Messi’s international future remained uncertain after the final, but the gift offered one clear message. The World Cup ended in disappointment. The squad still left with a reminder of the group that reached the final together.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi gave Argentina players personalized mate sets after the World Cup. The gift followed Argentina's painful loss to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. The collection included a custom bag, a gold-colored Stanley thermos, a mate cup, a metal straw and yerba mate.

Article Title: 'He's lying ... isn't sorry at all': Spain's Dani Olmo refuses to accept Argentina assistant coach's 'fake' apology
Article Text:
Spain's Dani Olmo (10) reacts during the World Cup semifinal soccer match between France and Spain in Arlington, Texas, near Dallas, Tuesday, July 14, 2026. (AP Photo/Abbie Parr)

Ayala's explanation prompts response from Olmo

Olmo: 'He's lying'

Diari de Terrassa

Spain want to be remembered for their conduct

Spain's Dani Olmo (10) celebrates with the trophy after the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)

Collective spirit behind Spain's triumph

Spain midfielder Dani Olmo has spoken publicly for the first time about the altercation that followed his side's 2026 FIFA World Cup final victory over Argentina, rejecting Roberto Ayala's apology and accusing the Argentina assistant coach of lying about what triggered the incident.The Barcelona midfielder became one of several Spain players caught up in the chaotic scenes that erupted after the final whistle in New Jersey, where Spain secured their second World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory thanks to Ferran Torres' decisive goal.FIFA has since opened disciplinary proceedings into Argentina's post-match conduct after a confrontation involving several players and members of the coaching staff.The disorder began after Nahuel Molina confronted Spain captain Rodri following the final whistle, with the exchange quickly escalating into a mass altercation involving players and staff from both teams.During the confrontation, television footage showed Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala making contact with Olmo as the Spain international stood alongside teammate Eric García.Earlier this week, Ayala acknowledged the incident while insisting it had been misunderstood.Speaking about the confrontation, the former Argentina defender said it had been "more of a shove than a punch" and claimed his reaction came in response to something Olmo had said.Ayala also indicated that he intended to apologise if he met the Spain midfielder in person.Speaking to, Olmo firmly rejected both Ayala's explanation and the apology."Someone who claims to be sorry, but justifies a punch by saying it was a response to a comment, probably isn't sorry at all," Olmo said.The Spain international then directly challenged Ayala's version of events."He's lying, because I didn't say anything to him, so I don't need him to apologise."Rather than focusing solely on the incident itself, Olmo said genuine accountability requires accepting responsibility without attempting to justify what happened."What truly defines us isn't the mistake, but the courage to own up to it with humility, honesty and dignity."His comments directly contradict Ayala's claim that the confrontation was provoked by remarks from the Spanish midfielder.Although the post-match scenes dominated much of the discussion after the final, Olmo said he hopes Spain's World Cup triumph will ultimately be remembered for the way the team conducted itself throughout the tournament."I want people to be proud of how we competed, how we won and, above all, of our behaviour," he said.The 27-year-old also reflected on the wider responsibility carried by elite footballers, particularly given the influence they have on younger supporters."The reach of football means that we players are role models for children and future generations, and that carries a great responsibility."Away from the controversy, Olmo highlighted the values he believes were central to Spain's World Cup-winning campaign."The group, the collective, always above individual players," he said, describing Luis de la Fuente's squad as a close-knit group built on teamwork rather than individual stardom.Olmo also praised the coaching and support staff, stressing that Spain's success was founded on months of meticulous preparation."It's all about hard work, nothing else, to achieve the goal."He explained that preparation extended well beyond training sessions on the pitch."The work isn't just physical. Invisible training is crucial, nutrition, rest, recovery, mental preparation, match analysis and healthy habits."According to Olmo, those elements formed the foundation of Spain's successful campaign, helping the team navigate the demands of the tournament before defeating Argentina to lift the World Cup for the second time in the nation's history.While FIFA's investigation into the post-match incidents remains ongoing, Olmo made clear that he believes Spain's lasting legacy from the tournament should be defined not by the confrontation after the final whistle, but by the football, discipline and collective spirit that carried them to the world title.
Article Summary: Dani Olmo has spoken publicly for the first time about the altercation that followed his side's 2026 FIFA World Cup final victory over Argentina. The Barcelona midfielder became one of several Spain players caught up in the chaotic scenes that erupted after the final whistle in New Jersey. Spain secured their second World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory thanks to Ferran Torres' decisive goal.
